title: The Sermon, looking back
tomorrow: is God found in the quiet room, or in the dishes?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Mark's trembling ending and its promise: he goes before you. Today, another ending, and this one comes with weather.
screen: `HE GOES BEFORE YOU.` → `AN ENDING WITH WEATHER.`

segments.voice: Two houses on a listing app, side by side. Same street, same paint, same view; on a sunny day nobody could tell them apart. Both builders even heard the same sermon. Then the rain comes, the floods rise, and the wind hits both walls at once, and one of them falls. That's how Jesus ends the Sermon on the Mount. Not with a summary. With weather. So what made the difference?
screen: `TWO HOUSES, ONE STREET.` → `SAME SERMON, SAME STORM.` → `ONE FALLS. WHY?`

segments.voice: Look back over the Sermon and it's full of pictures. It opens with blessings in unlikely places: “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” It hands ordinary listeners a job: “Ye are the salt of the earth.” “Ye are the light of the world.” Not you should become. You are. It points at a field: “Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin.” Then the ending: “Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.” The other builder hears the very same sayings, doesn't do them, and builds on sand. Here's the strange part, worth telling a friend: the storm hits both. Same rain, same floods, same wind, in almost the same words. Earlier in the same sermon, Jesus says God “sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.” Weather comes to everyone. So the wise builder isn't promised a dry life, and hearing isn't the difference either; both heard. The answer to the puzzle is the foundation, and the foundation is the doing: “and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.” A sermon can be framed on a wall and still not be lived. And rock is there for anyone who does the next saying, even one.
screen: `BLESSED, SALT, LIGHT, LILIES.` · `BOTH BUILDERS HEARD.` · `THE RAIN FALLS ON BOTH.` · `THE DIFFERENCE IS THE DOING.` · then, large: `BUILD ON ROCK.`

segments.voice: Write one line from the Sermon by hand, on a card or a scrap of paper: blessed are the poor in spirit, ye are the light of the world, consider the lilies, or another. Choose the one you could actually do this week, and put it where you'll see it. If you pray, ask for help doing it, not only hearing it.
The Sermon. Jesus's long teaching on the mount in Matthew, from blessed to rock, ending with two houses in one storm.
Pocket this one: build on rock; the rain falls on both houses, and the doing is the foundation. See you tomorrow.

fork.setup: your friend has 'blessed are the peacemakers' framed in her room, and she's in the middle of a fight with her sister. what does the Sermon's ending suggest?
options: the frame matters most; having the words up is the main thing.
make one move toward peace; the house stands on doing, not hearing.

fork.reveal: both builders heard the same sayings. the one who did them built on rock, and the house stood through the same storm.

chat.meaning: Both builders in Matthew 7 heard the same sayings; the one who did them built on rock. And the rain falls on both houses.

Sermon on the Mount.meaning: Jesus's long teaching in Matthew, chapters five to seven

poor in spirit.meaning: those who know they need God

lilies.meaning: wildflowers of the field, in Jesus's picture against worry

the just and on the unjust.meaning: good people and bad people alike
